newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia introduces compulsory vehicle insurance.
newsitem.headline: Latvia introduces compulsory vehicle insurance.

text.p: Latvia's parliament on Thursday passed a new law that for the first time introduces compulsory motor vehicle insurance but set the premiums at rates below those demanded by insurance companies.
The new insurance rules come into effect on August 1, the parliament press office said.
In a controversial move, parliament decided to cut the tariffs by half from the ones proposed in the initial draft law.
The tariff for cars is 20 lats a year against the proposed 50 and 36 lats for trucks against the suggested 70.
Tariffs on other categories, including buses, motorbikes and trams and trolleybuses have also been reduced by half.
All of Latvia's eight insurance companies have already said they would refuse to insure motor vehicles at such tariffs would cause losses to the industry of around five million lats.
Estonia has already introduced compulsory insurance but insurance companies there also asked for premiums to be raised as they were at first too low.
